Exposition: That thing was prepared for you, with the nums in squares, tons, and streets; an internal praise for you as well, where the priest would serve you. But you did not want it. So this is a really important idea. The reality is constructed through our own imagination, a hallucination. Everyone lives in someone else's imagination, and these laws were created by others. However, what this means is that you can create your own reality. When you do, people will obey your laws.

Think of the story: This is about a nun sworn to uphold church rules. Frank undressed, lay in bed, and imagined her coming. She did come, undressed, and lay beside him. She was afraid she would be punished by God if she had sex with this man, but he assured her it was okay. The world you make is what you imagine. If you train your mind to see the world a certain way, everyone else will see it that way.

But if you create your own world inside your head without influencing others, how can you make them follow? Only someone with an imagination can do this. Think of a writer imagining and writing down their world. When you read the book, you come into this world. Similarly, in a television show, you think it's real because someone made up this reality.

So, train your mind through constant education, reading, dialogue, and debate. Frames are powerful because they're people deeply engaged in learning and exercising their imagination. Frank’s followers, mostly Jews, will convert to Catholicism for more opportunities. Before converting, they have a ceremony: the Lord sets up a garden, undresses with his followers, and orders everyone to do so. He drives a nail into the center, hangs candles, and bows before it. Afterward, sexual relations take place.

One woman laughed, and he ordered the candles extinguished. With this deed, they go naked, converting to a new religion and swearing loyalty to each other through a ritual of love. This ritual empowers them to go far and wide.
